Applies the transfer function directly to the input volume to create an opacity volume, preserving volumetric shape and allowing combination with any feature tensor.
Uses a TF Extractor (1D CNN) to produce a low-dimensional feature vector (descriptor) from the transfer function, which is injected into the network.
*   **Time Complexity:** Inference time is dominated by the 3D CNN forward pass.
*   **Memory Complexity:** VRAM usage is high due to the 3D CNN weights and intermediate feature maps.
*   **When to use:** When high-quality volumetric illumination is required and the transfer function changes infrequently, allowing for pre-computation.
Suitable for interactive visualization where the cost of re-computing AO numerically is prohibitive.
*   **When not to use:** When memory is constrained or real-time performance for every frame (including volume changes) is critical without pre-computation.
Not suitable for very high-resolution volumes without significant architectural changes.

The method addresses the limitations of traditional numerical ambient occlusion in volume rendering by leveraging deep learning to predict the AO field, building on the principles of [Neural volume rendering](1576-neural-volume-rendering.md).
